items.title: Signs Your Manual Gearbox Needs Attention
items.description: Manual gearboxes rarely fail suddenly - they give you warning signs. Here's what to look for.

cards.title: Grinding into gear
cards.text: Synchromesh wear, clutch not fully disengaging
cards.fullText: Grinding into gear Synchromesh wear, clutch not fully disengaging ⚠️ Get checked - driving may worsen damage

cards.title: Popping out of gear
cards.text: Worn synchromesh, damaged shift forks, worn detent springs
cards.fullText: Popping out of gear Worn synchromesh, damaged shift forks, worn detent springs ⚠️ Get checked - could fail completely

cards.title: Difficulty selecting reverse
cards.text: Worn synchromesh (reverse), clutch drag, cable adjustment
cards.fullText: Difficulty selecting reverse Worn synchromesh (reverse), clutch drag, cable adjustment ⚠️ Get checked - early indicator of wear

cards.title: Whining or rumbling noise
cards.text: Worn bearings, low fluid, damaged gears
cards.fullText: Whining or rumbling noise Worn bearings, low fluid, damaged gears ⚠️ Get checked - progressive wear

cards.title: Clutch pedal feel changed
cards.text: Hydraulic issue, clutch wear, pressure plate failure
cards.fullText: Clutch pedal feel changed Hydraulic issue, clutch wear, pressure plate failure ⚠️ Get checked - could leave you stranded

cards.title: Gear lever feels sloppy
cards.text: Worn linkage, shift cables, bushes
cards.fullText: Gear lever feels sloppy Worn linkage, shift cables, bushes ⚠️ Get checked - will get worse

cards.title: Burning smell from gearbox
cards.text: Overheated fluid, worn components, clutch slipping
cards.fullText: Burning smell from gearbox Overheated fluid, worn components, clutch slipping 🔴 Stop driving - possible fire risk

cards.title: Leaking fluid
cards.text: Seals worn, damaged casing
cards.fullText: Leaking fluid Seals worn, damaged casing ⚠️ Get checked - low fluid causes internal wear

cards.title: Loud grinding / clunking
cards.text: Loud grinding / clunking Internal damage - driving could destroy the gearbox.
cards.fullText: Loud grinding / clunking Internal damage - driving could destroy the gearbox.

cards.title: Complete loss of drive
cards.text: Complete loss of drive Major internal failure - driving is impossible.
cards.fullText: Complete loss of drive Major internal failure - driving is impossible.

cards.title: Burning smell
cards.text: Burning smell Overheated fluid or clutch - stop driving immediately.
cards.fullText: Burning smell Overheated fluid or clutch - stop driving immediately.

cards.title: Gearbox seized
cards.text: Gearbox seized Complete failure - do not attempt to drive.
cards.fullText: Gearbox seized Complete failure - do not attempt to drive.

items.title: Repair vs Replacement Decision Framework
items.description: Use this framework to decide whether to repair or replace your manual gearbox.

cards.text: ⚠️ Grinding into gear, no metal in oil Repair or replace - synchromesh wear, may be repairable
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Grinding into gear, no metal in oil Repair or replace - synchromesh wear, may be repairable

cards.text: ⚠️ Popping out of gear, difficulty selecting Replace - internal wear, likely beyond repair
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Popping out of gear, difficulty selecting Replace - internal wear, likely beyond repair

cards.text: ⚠️ Whining noise, low fluid Repair - top up fluid, inspect bearings
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Whining noise, low fluid Repair - top up fluid, inspect bearings

cards.text: ❌ Loud grinding, metal in oil Replace - internal damage is extensive
cards.fullText: ❌ Loud grinding, metal in oil Replace - internal damage is extensive

cards.fullText: ❌ Complete loss of drive Replace - major internal failure

cards.fullText: ✅ Clutch slipping (gear changes difficult) Repair - replace clutch only (not gearbox)

items.title: Anecdotal Validation from UK Specialists
items.description: The following insights are drawn from interviews with UK gearbox specialists [EM-INTERVIEW] .

blocks.text: "A manual gearbox is simpler than an automatic - fewer components, no hydraulics, no electronics. But it still needs proper inspection and specialist knowledge. The most common mistake is ignoring the early warning signs - a slight crunch or a difficult shift."

"Most manual gearbox problems are actually clutch problems. A slipping clutch, a clutch that's dragging, a clutch that's not fully disengaging - these cause grinding and difficult shifts. The gearbox itself is often fine. If the clutch is replaced in time, the gearbox can last the life of the car."

"Manual gearboxes are readily available used - there are millions of them in breakers across the UK. But not all used gearboxes are good. We always ask: what was the mileage? What was the donor vehicle? What's the warranty? A £400 used gearbox might cost you £800 in labour - and another £800 if it fails."

blocks.question: How much does manual gearbox replacement cost? −
blocks.answer: 5-speed manual £500-£1,500 , 6-speed manual £800-£2,500 , heavy-duty £1,200-£4,000 , performance £1,500-£5,000 . Prices vary by gearbox type, condition, and vehicle.

blocks.question: Should I replace the clutch at the same time? +
blocks.answer: Yes - if the gearbox is being replaced, the labour is already being done. You'll save £200-£300 in labour by replacing the clutch now rather than later.

blocks.question: What's the difference between used, reconditioned, and new? +
blocks.answer: Used - removed from donor vehicle, sold as-is. Reconditioned - fully dismantled, inspected, worn parts replaced, tested. New - brand new from manufacturer, most expensive.

blocks.question: What are the signs of manual gearbox failure? +
blocks.answer: Grinding into gear, popping out of gear, difficulty selecting reverse, whining noise, clutch pedal feel changed, gear lever feels sloppy.

blocks.question: How long does manual gearbox replacement take? +
blocks.answer: Labour typically takes 4-8 hours (1 day) . Additional time for sourcing the gearbox. Allow 2-5 days for the complete process.

blocks.question: What warranty comes with a manual gearbox replacement? +
blocks.answer: Used: 1-3 months. Reconditioned: 3-12 months. New: 12-24 months. Always check the specific terms with your supplier.

blocks.question: Is manual gearbox replacement cheaper than automatic? +
blocks.answer: Yes - manual gearboxes are simpler, have fewer components, and require less labour. Typical manual replacement costs £500-£3,000 vs automatic £1,000-£5,000 .

blocks.question: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer? +
blocks.answer: Gearbox replacement doesn't require DVLA notification. You should check with your insurer - some policies require notification of major mechanical changes.
